deep.reconstruction:
There are no computations or derivations on this page. It is a page of aphoristic notes from Hilbert's notebook, continuing the series on the previous and next pages (Lie, Riemann, Weierstrass, Cauchy; 'three kinds of scientific pleasure'; 'grau, theurer Freund, ist alle Theorie'; the 'two legs' of quantity and form). The page contains four entries.

(1) End of a sentence from p.95, on physicists' preference for approximation over exact limiting statements: '...in the unconscious fear that it might be impossible for the human understanding to recognise the inner connection.'

(2) 'Mathematics is the science of divisibility and of greater/smaller, or of the concept "between".' This names two primitive kinds of structure. Divisibility is the arithmetical/algebraic side: number theory and reducibility, as on p.97. Greater/smaller/between is the order or magnitude side: analysis, geometry and physics. It anticipates the 'two legs' aphorism on p.97.

(3) 'Geometry = arithmetic, because ... whether I say greater or smaller or whether I say between is really all the same. If one grasps the relation of arithmetic and geometry more deeply, one perceives no difference. Geometry can be built up completely rigorously. The theorem on the existence of roots can be proved completely rigorously by purely geometric means.'
- Modern reading: a linear order (<) and a betweenness relation are interdefinable up to orientation. Hilbert's later axioms of order (Grundlagen der Geometrie, 1899) take 'zwischen' as primitive; the segment arithmetic built on them makes geometry and ordered-field arithmetic equivalent.
- 'Wurzelexistenz' is most plausibly the existence of roots of polynomials (the fundamental theorem of algebra, as in Gauss's 1799 curve-intersection proof). It could also mean existence of real roots via continuity or betweenness, or of square roots via constructions. No proof is given.

(4) 'Transcendence of e and pi, invariant-theoretic counting methods were only the tendernesses of an engagement. Here, in the theory of class fields (complex multiplication), number theory and function theory celebrate their wedding.'
- The first items refer to Hilbert's own work: his 1893 simplification of the Hermite–Lindemann transcendence proofs and his invariant-theoretic counting arguments of 1890–93. These are cases where analytic or functional methods touch arithmetic.
- The 'wedding' is complex multiplication. Values of elliptic and modular functions at imaginary quadratic arguments, such as j(tau), generate abelian extensions (class fields) of imaginary quadratic fields. This is Kronecker's Jugendtraum, and it is the programme Hilbert later stated as Problem 12 (1900), where he speaks of the most intimate connection of number theory, algebra and function theory.
- The term 'Klassenkörper' places the note in the late 1890s (Hilbert 1898–1902).
errors: No mathematical errors, since no computations are made.

'Geometrie = Arithmetik' because greater/smaller and 'between' are 'einerlei' is a philosophical simplification. Betweenness does not by itself recover an ordered field; that needs further axioms (congruence, parallels, Archimedes or completeness), as Hilbert himself later showed.

The claim that root existence can be proved 'rein geometrisch völlig streng' was optimistic by the rigour standards of the 1890s if the fundamental theorem of algebra is meant. Gauss's geometric proof had a topological gap that was only closed later (Ostrowski 1920).

results.what: Mathematics characterised as the science of divisibility (algebraic structure) and of order/betweenness (magnitude)
results.modern_name: Dichotomy of algebraic vs. order/topological structure (cf. Bourbaki's mother structures)
results.usually_credited_to: Bourbaki (1940s–50) for the structural taxonomy; the sentiment is common earlier

results.what: Geometry is equivalent to arithmetic; betweenness is equivalent to order; geometry can be built fully rigorously
results.modern_name: Arithmetisation of geometry via order axioms and segment arithmetic
results.usually_credited_to: Pasch (1882) for betweenness axioms; Hilbert, Grundlagen der Geometrie (1899)

results.what: Existence of roots provable purely geometrically
results.modern_name: Fundamental theorem of algebra (geometric/topological proof) or intermediate value property
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss 1799 (geometric proof); rigorous topological completion by Ostrowski 1920

results.what: Complex multiplication as the 'marriage' of number theory and function theory in class field theory
results.modern_name: Kronecker's Jugendtraum / Hilbert's 12th problem / theory of complex multiplication

deep.surprise_reason: These are philosophical aphorisms, not new results. The views match Hilbert's published positions: the Grundlagen der Geometrie, the 1900 Paris address (Problem 12's 'innigste Beziehung'), and his transcendence and invariant work. The Verlobung/Vermählung metaphor is a nice private formulation, but excerpts of these notebooks have been discussed by historians (e.g. Rowe). It is of mild biographical and dating interest only.
